official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 current radon dataset
official_measurement_examples.fact: The BGS National Data Library record for Radon Potential for Great Britain version 3 was updated on 23 July 2026 and describes the joint UKHSA-BGS dataset as the current definitive map of Radon Affected Areas in Great Britain.

official_measurement_examples.name: Affected Area threshold
official_measurement_examples.fact: UKHSA defines Radon Affected Areas as areas where there is at least a 1% chance of a house having an annual average radon concentration at or above the 200 Bq/m3 Action Level.

official_measurement_examples.name: Indicative atlas limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The free indicative atlas classifies each 1-km grid square by the highest radon potential within it, so the atlas class is not a definitive property-level measurement.

official_measurement_examples.name: Definitive versus indicative
official_measurement_examples.fact: The detailed Radon Potential Dataset provides the definitive affected-area status, while the public atlas is a simplified overview; the two must not be treated as identical spatial evidence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building protective measures
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building-regulation guidance can require no, basic or full radon protective measures depending on assessed radon potential; the mapped risk class does not prove those measures have actually been designed or installed on a parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Measurement distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A radon-potential map estimates probability from measurements and geology; an actual building's annual average radon level requires measurement and must not be inferred as a precise Bq/m3 value from the map alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Workplace context
official_measurement_examples.fact: HSE guidance uses radon affected-area information to identify where workplace assessment or testing may be needed; affected-area status is not a planning permission or planning-refusal rule.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Radon potential does not establish ownership, planning permission, exact buildable area, mitigation cost or final development yield without proposal-specific building and ground evidence.

core_rules: radon potential map is not measured building concentration
indicative 1km atlas is not definitive property status
200 Bq/m3 action level is not a mapped parcel measurement
radon affected area is not automatic planning refusal
radon affected area is not planning permission
building-regulation protective requirement is not proof measures are installed
Approved Document guidance is not site-specific compliance certificate
workplace radon assessment is distinct from land-use permission
map update date is not building measurement date
radon potential does not establish ownership
radon potential does not calculate parcel yield
mitigation feasibility and cost require site/building evidence
no parcel radon clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official BGS/National Data Library, UKHSA/UKradon, HSE, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked on 2026-07-26. 23 July 2026 dataset currentity retained with definitive/indicative, probability/measurement and building-regulation/planning separation; no parcel promotion.
